fields.statement: Plan review round 3 left finding f1 (contradiction on web-host-setting-shape): The change set's intent says it supersedes only 'the localhost part' of Decision web-ui-in-daemon-read-only, but the plan adds a supersedes link from web-host-setting-shape to that whole decision. That decision also carries the owner's quoted 'First pass will be read only. For monitoring purposes only' and still decides milestone-28 and web-monitor; web-host-setting-shape restates only the host and read-only allowlist, not the monitoring-only scope or its quote, so superseding the whole decision retires owner-quoted provenance the intent keeps. Either supersede with a narrower statement that explicitly carries the unchanged parts (with derived-from to the original decision) or drop the supersedes link and record the localhost change as an amendment. The critic confirmed it: The supersedes link 01M6QCGW5VASCCZX5JR0XDBW7V does carry a note limiting it to the localhost clause, but the model ignores that note: internal/slice/rules.go:203 drops any decision with a live incoming supersedes link. rhiza slice web-monitor --change 01M6QBS no longer lists web-ui-in-daemon-read-only, and web-host-setting-shape does not decide web-monitor, milestone-28, web-api-read-only, web-events-stream, web-templates-embedded, web-live-sections, web-roadmap-page or web-change-set-page. So those capabilities lose the owner-quoted read-only, monitoring-only decision from their slices, which the intent ('The UI stays read-only') keeps. The fix must keep that decision current for them: drop the supersedes link and amend, or supersede with a narrower decision that restates the unchanged parts, derives from the original and decides the same capabilities. How should it be settled?
